subject: Physics
description: Reflection laws, mirror types (plane, concave, convex), images, applications

questions.stem: FIRST LAW OF REFLECTION states that:

options.option_text: Angle of incidence > angle of reflection
Angle of incidence = angle of reflection (equal)
Light always travels in straight line

questions.explanation: LAWS OF REFLECTION: (1) Angle of INCIDENCE = Angle of REFLECTION (both measured from NORMAL, the perpendicular at point of contact). (2) Incident ray, reflected ray, normal — ALL LIE IN THE SAME PLANE. INSIGHT — these laws apply to EVERY type of mirror (plane, concave, convex) and every smooth reflecting surface, even WATER + glass. WHY mirrors work: smooth surface → all parallel rays reflect at same angle (REGULAR reflection). Rough surface → rays scatter (DIFFUSE reflection — why we can see non-mirror objects). Distractor 3 is REFRACTION (light bending when entering different medium — Snell's law).

questions.stem: An image formed by a PLANE MIRROR is:

options.option_text: Virtual, erect, same size, laterally inverted

questions.explanation: PLANE MIRROR image: VIRTUAL (formed BEHIND mirror; rays only appear to come from there but don't actually meet); ERECT (upright); SAME SIZE as object; LATERALLY INVERTED (left-right swap; that's why letters appear backwards in mirror — try writing your name + see it in mirror). DISTANCE: image is at SAME distance behind mirror as object is in front. EXAM PYQ: AMBULANCE writes its name MIRROR-REVERSED so that drivers ahead, looking in their rear-view mirror, see it correctly! REAL vs VIRTUAL — real images can be projected on screen (formed by actual ray convergence); virtual cannot (rays only appear to converge).

questions.stem: A CONCAVE mirror is used as:
questions.explanation: CONCAVE mirror = converging mirror (curves IN, like inside of spoon). USES: (1) SHAVING mirror — when face is INSIDE focal length, image is VIRTUAL, ERECT, MAGNIFIED (you see yourself bigger). (2) Headlight / TORCH reflector — bulb at FOCUS produces parallel reflected beam (high-intensity directional light). (3) Solar cookers + furnaces (concentrate sunlight at focus). (4) Doctor's HEAD MIRROR (forehead-mounted, focuses light into ear/throat). (5) Telescope (Newtonian / Cassegrain types). CONVEX mirror — diverging; gives wider field of view (used in vehicle rear-view, road junctions, ATM corners). REVERSE EXAM TRAP: rear-view mirrors are CONVEX (not concave).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A CONVEX mirror always forms images that are:
questions.explanation: CONVEX mirror = diverging (curves OUT). ALWAYS forms VIRTUAL, ERECT, DIMINISHED images, regardless of object position. Image lies between pole + focus (behind mirror). DIMINISHED → covers WIDER FIELD OF VIEW in same mirror size — that's why used in: rear-view mirrors of vehicles (legal warning: 'objects in mirror are CLOSER than they appear' — because diminished image makes them seem far); ATM CORNERS, ROAD CURVES, store-corner SECURITY mirrors (one mirror sees entire aisle). KEY DIFFERENCE: concave can form 6 different image types (real/virtual, erect/inverted, magnified/diminished) depending on object distance; convex always one type.

questions.stem: FOCAL LENGTH (f) and RADIUS OF CURVATURE (R) of a spherical mirror are related by:
questions.explanation: For SPHERICAL MIRRORS (small aperture, paraxial approximation): f = R/2 (focal length is HALF the radius of curvature). RADIUS = distance from POLE to centre of curvature; FOCUS lies midway between. Sign convention: CONCAVE → f, R both NEGATIVE (in front of mirror, by Cartesian convention); CONVEX → f, R both POSITIVE. INSIGHT — for LENSES, the relation is different: f depends on both surface radii + refractive index (lens-maker's equation). LARGE-APERTURE mirrors deviate from f = R/2 due to spherical aberration → use parabolic mirrors for telescopes.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: MIRROR FORMULA relating object distance (u), image distance (v), focal length (f) is:
questions.explanation: MIRROR FORMULA: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. Sign convention (Cartesian): distances measured from POLE; positive if in same direction as incident light, negative otherwise. So for concave mirror: u is negative (object in front); f is negative; v is negative (real image in front) or positive (virtual image behind). MAGNIFICATION m = −v/u = h_image / h_object. INSIGHT — same FORM applies to thin LENSES too (with sign convention adjusted: lens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f). PYQ TIP: practice sign convention carefully — wrong sign is the most common mistake.

questions.stem: Periscope (used in submarines + tanks) primarily uses:

options.option_text: Just one large flat plane mirror

questions.explanation: PERISCOPE — uses TWO PARALLEL plane mirrors, each tilted 45° to the line of sight. Light from above (e.g., surface) hits TOP mirror → reflects down through tube → hits BOTTOM mirror → reflects horizontally to viewer's eye. Used in: submarines (to see above water while underwater); tanks (driver to see outside while protected); trench warfare (seeing over walls). IMAGE in periscope = same size, erect, SAME orientation (no lateral inversion because two reflections cancel). INSIGHT — modern periscopes use PRISMS (using TIR — total internal reflection) for sharper images. Submarines now use ELECTRONIC PERISCOPES (cameras + monitors) — no mast through the hull.
